title: Food and Digestion
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Food and Digestion Worksheets (Nutrients, Enzymes, Energy)
standard_text: Content of a healthy human diet: carbohydrates, lipids (fats and oils), proteins, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre and water, and why each is needed; calculations of energy requirements in a healthy daily diet; the consequences of imbalances in the diet, including obesity, starvation and deficiency diseases; the tissues and organs of the human digestive system, including adaptations to function and how the digestive system digests food (enzymes simply as biological catalysts); the importance of bacteria in the human digestive system.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on food and digestion: nutrients, deficiency diseases, energy in food, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Enzymes break big molecules into small ones.
key_sub: Nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine; a balanced diet has seven food groups.
body_html:
How to think about it

A balanced diet gives the body the right amounts of seven food groups.

  • Carbohydrates and lipids give energy, proteins build and repair, vitamins and minerals keep us healthy, fibre helps digestion, water is needed by every cell.
  • Enzymes break big molecules into small ones: amylase → starch, protease → protein, lipase → lipid.
  • Nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine; water in the large intestine.
Example

Energy in 50 g of a food with 1,600 kJ per 100 g?

1,600 × 50 ÷ 100

Answer: 800 kJ

Example

Which enzyme digests protein?

Prote-

Answer: protease

Common mistakes

  • Thinking enzymes are alive.
  • Thinking digestion happens only in the stomach.
  • Thinking fibre is digested for energy.

faq.q: What are the parts of a balanced diet?
faq.a: Carbohydrates, lipids (fats and oils), proteins, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre and water, in the right amounts.
They break large food molecules into small ones: amylase breaks starch into sugars, protease breaks proteins into amino acids and lipase breaks lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.

faq.q: How do you calculate the energy in a portion?
faq.a: Multiply the energy per 100 g by the mass of the portion and divide by 100.
